connector.why: Purim's 'yekar' = head-tefillin and Malchut/'malchut peh' = Oral Torah of the sages; shares the Malchut-Oral Torah-yekar chain but not the Esther/Sarah or every-Jew theme.

connector.why: Rabbi Akiva as foundation of the Oral Torah, with 'kol yekar' (Bamidbar Rabbah 19:6) and 'kulhu aliba d'R. Akiva' (Sanhedrin 86a): the same sub-argument, set in a discussion of the unfolding of Oral Torah.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:30
connector.why: Moshe root of Written Torah vs. Rabbi Akiva as foundation of Oral Torah, 'kol yekar' and Sanhedrin 86a; but yekar is read as tikkun of keri, a different thrust.

Almost the same chain as the Malchut section: Arizal that R. Akiva is root of Oral Torah, proved from Sanhedrin 86a, Moshe = Written Torah, Ramban on Bava Batra 12 (ruach hakodesh), 'malchut peh', and 'kol yekar' (Chukat midrash).
R. Akiva's 'kol yekar' (things not revealed to Moshe) and the post-Churban growth of Oral Torah tied to Purim; shares the Oral-Torah strand only.
R. Akiva's attainment by wisdom = 'kol yekar', with Megillah 16b yekar = head-tefillin; the yekar/tefillin step of the maamar, developed toward Aramaic and the Zohar.
Cites chacham adif minavi and 'kol yekar' for R. Akiva, but the passage is about vision vs. completed action (Ben Azzai vs. R. Akiva), not Oral Torah/Malchut.
Sages' ruach hakodesh (Bava Batra 12a with Ramban) and 'kol yekar' for R. Akiva; same link of Oral Torah to ruach hakodesh, within a Shabbat/prophecy discussion.
Ramban on Bava Batra 12a (sages' ruach hakodesh), R. Akiva and 'kol yekar'; but the focus is halacha l'Moshe miSinai and Aharon/Hod.
Oral Torah drawn by ruach hakodesh (Rashi's 'daat', Ramban Bava Batra 12a) and 'kol yekar'; Keter/crowns follow; Chanukah setting.

R. Akiva root of Oral Torah, sage's ruach hakodesh per Ramban on Bava Batra 12a, 'yekar = tefillin' on the head, and 'kol yekar' (Chukat midrash): the same chain as the maamar's Malchut section; already in fn 22/28.

connector.ref: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 16:33
connector.why: Esther going in 'asher lo kadat', karka olam (Sanhedrin 74), 've-ka'asher avadti avadti' as readiness to lose even the World to Come: the same Esther-self-sacrifice section, read differently.

Uses 'ra'mot le-evil chochmot' for the yetzer making Torah feel beyond one's power, and teaches that Anochi precedes Lo yihyeh so that everyone can enter Torah though not yet clean of evil: the maamar's thesis.

Amalek's 'coldness': 'what can I attain with my small grasp... ra'mot le-evil chochmot', despair that loosens Torah; same diagnosis as the dozing congregation, different remedy (zeal, and God completes).

connector.ref: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, Novellae, Rif, Shabbat 4:1
connector.why: Proves one may give his life beyond the obligation from Ketubot 3b 'tzenuot' though a woman is karka olam (Sanhedrin 74b): the same halachic point Rav Tzadok makes for Esther.

candidates.why: Asks Rav Tzadok's exact question (why wake them with this derasha, and why R. Akiva); answers (§76) that R. Akiva's derasha aims to bind himself to his dozing generation and raise them, which needs their will: close in purpose, different mechanism.

candidates.ref: Notes by Rabbi Yehoshua Hartman on Ohr Chadash 1:1:134-137
candidates.why: Only quotes the midrash to explain why Maharal compares Sarah's years with the 127 provinces; nothing on why the congregation was woken or on every Jew's share.

candidates.ref: Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 1-4
candidates.why: Explains the same waking: the dozing is weariness from hester panim (exile); Esther = hiddenness, yet she reigns by Sarah's merit, so they should trust God in the dark. Same question, different answer (and fn 36 already notes its 'kulan shavin le-tovah' as a contrast).

Nearly Rav Tzadok's reading: R. Akiva expounded lofty things and people dozed because they thought they could not live up to them; he woke them with Sarah, whose years even at 100 like 20 were all sanctified, though she was exempt from time-bound mitzvot.
A running commentary on the Megillah narrative (Haman, Charbona, the letters); shares only the words 'bedidah'/'shelevashtah', nothing of the maamar's idea.

found.why: Reads the Tanna Devei Eliyahu obligation exactly as Rav Tzadok's ending does: it forbids the false humility of 'who am I to seek great things', which the Satan plants to idle a person from Torah.
In the name of the Pshischa: no fool compares himself to the Patriarchs; 'yagi'u' means one's deeds touch and cleave to the Patriarchs' deeds; parallels Rav Tzadok's 'at least in some particular'.

'The deeds of my fathers that they planted in me': the Patriarchs prepared knowledge and longing for all Israel, to be awakened in their offspring; Rav Tzadok's 'they planted in the heart of their offspring'.

States the same equation Rav Tzadok draws from Esther's verse: ruach hakodesh is the aspect of Malchut ('va-tilbash Esther malchut... she was clothed in ruach hakodesh'), applied to Torah and prayer spoken in attachment to Malchut.

footnotes.text: **Derekh HaMelekh, Chayei Sarah 2:17–18** (Chassidus) — The same reading of the midrash: the people dozed because they thought R. Akiva's lofty teaching was beyond their service; he woke them with Sarah, who sanctified all her years though exempt from time-bound mitzvot. כי חשבו שכיון שר"ע דורש כ"כ דברים גבוהים א"א להם לקיים ולעבוד בהם בתמימות

**Ben Porat Yosef, Chayei Sarah 64, 76** (Chassidus) — Asks Rav Tzadok's question (why this derasha, and why R. Akiva) and answers that R. Akiva's derasha binds him to the dozing people to raise them, if they are willing. ולכך דרש דרוש זה דוקא, כדי לעוררן ולהודיען שרוצה להעלותן בדרוש זה

footnotes.ref: Chiddushei HaRim on Torah, Chayei Sara 2
footnotes.text: **Chiddushei HaRim, Chayei Sarah 2** (Chassidus) — Another answer to the same question: the dozing is weariness under hester panim; Esther, whose name means hiddenness, reigns by Sarah's merit, so R. Akiva woke them to trust God even in the dark. כי מה שהאדם נעשה עיף בעבודת השי"ת ובא לידי ביטול ושינה הוא ע"י הסתרת פנים

**Sefat Emet, Bamidbar 1:3** (Chassidus) — In the name of the Pshischa: no one can equal the Patriarchs, but his deeds can "reach" (touch and cleave to) theirs; like Rav Tzadok's "in some particular." אך פי' יגיעו שיהי' למעשיו נגיעה ודביקות וחיבור במעשה אבות

**Sefat Emet, Vayera 30:4** (Chassidus) — Reads the Tanna Devei Eliyahu as "the deeds of my fathers that they planted in me": the Patriarchs prepared a longing in all their offspring that each can awaken, as Rav Tzadok says here. פירוש למעשה אבותי שנטעו בי

**Be'er Mayim Chaim, Bereishis 27:3** (Chassidus) — The obligation to say "when will my deeds reach" forbids the false humility of "who am I" that idles a person from Torah. This is the voice Rav Tzadok tells the listener not to heed. כי לא יעצל בענוה של שקר לומר מי אני לעבוד כל כך ולבקש גדולות ונפלאות

**Likutei Moharan I 78:3** (Chassidus) — Draws the same equation from the same Gemara: ruach hakodesh is Malchut, since "Esther clothed herself in royalty" means ruach hakodesh clothed her. וְרוּחַ־הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא בְּחִינוֹת מַלְכוּת
